title: Eurostar staff strike over pay and working conditions

tea.why: Staff are protesting over pay, working conditions, and the company's decision to host a luxury farewell event for the outgoing CEO.
tea.want: Employees are demanding better pay, improved working conditions, and increased recognition.
tea.changed: Nov 25: The strike caused multiple train cancellations between London, Paris, and Lille.

summary: On November 25, 2026, Eurostar staff initiated a strike that resulted in significant disruptions to rail services between London, Paris, and Lille. The industrial action was organised by the FO-Cheminots union, which stated that the walkout was a response to stalled annual pay negotiations and deteriorating working conditions. Protesters also cited a luxury farewell event for the outgoing CEO as a point of contention. Eurostar reported that the strike was unexpected and led to the cancellation of several services, advising passengers to avoid stations. While the company stated it remains open to constructive dialogue, union representatives described the social dialogue as broken. The strike saw high participation rates among drivers and station staff in Paris and Lille, with an assembly planned to discuss potential continuation of the movement.
response: Eurostar stated it was informed of the action overnight and apologised for the inconvenience. The company advised passengers to rebook or seek refunds and noted that it remains willing to engage in constructive dialogue with the union.

updates.text: Eurostar staff launched a strike, leading to the cancellation of several trains between London and Paris.
The FO-Cheminots union reported high participation rates among staff in Paris and Lille.
